text: Men are much more unwilling to have their weaknesses and their imperfections known than their crimes; and if you hint to a man that you think him silly, ignorant, or even ill-bred, or awkward, he will hate you more and longer, than if you tell him plainly, that you think him a rogue.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XLIX, to his son, London, September 5, Old Style 1748
